1 | # Bobtention for VS Code
2 | 
3 | One-click workspace setup and hook management for [Bobtention](https://github.com/suwasto/bobtention) — the human attention router for IBM Bob.
4 | 
5 | ## Features
6 | 
7 | - **One-Click Workspace Setup:** Run `Bobtention: Initialize Workspace` from the Command Palette (`Ctrl+Shift+P` / `Cmd+Shift+P`).
8 |   - Automatically merges the 5 required hooks (`SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `Stop`) into `.bob/settings.json`.
9 |   - Creates a default `bobtention.config.json` if absent.
10 |   - Prepares `~/.bobtention/` and workspace session/log storage.
11 | - **Hook Removal / Reset:** Run `Bobtention: Remove Hooks from Workspace` to cleanly detach Bobtention from your `.bob/settings.json` without altering other settings.
12 | 
13 | ## Usage
14 | 
15 | 1. Open your project folder in VS Code.
16 | 2. Open Command Palette: `Cmd+Shift+P` (macOS) or `Ctrl+Shift+P` (Windows/Linux).
17 | 3. Type and select **`Bobtention: Initialize Workspace`**.
18 | 4. That's it! Your IBM Bob sessions in this workspace will now run with Bobtention attention routing.
19 | 
20 | ## Development & Publishing
21 | 
22 | ### Compile
23 | ```bash
24 | npm install
25 | npm run compile
26 | ```
27 | 
28 | ### Package into .vsix
29 | ```bash
30 | npm run package
31 | ```
32 | 
33 | ### Install locally
34 | ```bash
35 | code --install-extension bobtention-vscode-0.1.0.vsix
36 | ```
37 | 
38 | ### Publish to VS Code Marketplace
39 | ```bash
40 | npx @vscode/vsce publish
41 | ```
42 |

Contents of file README.md:

1 | # Bobtention
2 | 
3 | > **Human attention router for IBM Bob.** Lets Bob work autonomously and interrupts you only when the session gives a meaningful reason to pay attention.
4 | 
5 | Bobtention runs as a set of [IBM Bob](https://www.ibm.com/bob) hook scripts. It tracks the trajectory of every Bob coding session — task alignment, progress, scope, action impact, and uncertainty — and routes attention using an **Allow / Watch / Block** decision model. When Bob is working normally Bobtention stays invisible. When Bob gets stuck, drifts off task, or reaches a high-impact action, Bobtention stops Bob and explains why.
6 | 
7 | ---
8 | 
9 | ## How It Works
10 | 
11 | ```
12 | Developer prompt
13 |       │
14 |       ▼
15 |  UserPromptSubmit ──→ capture intent
16 |       │
17 |       ▼ (for each tool use)
18 |   PreToolUse ──→ evaluate ──→ ALLOW → continue
19 |                           └──→ WATCH → continue + log
20 |                           └──→ BLOCK → stop + explain
21 |       │
22 |   PostToolUse ──→ observe outcome, accumulate signals
23 |       │
24 |     Stop ──→ finalize session
25 | ```
26 | 
27 | **Decision model**
28 | 
29 | | Decision | Meaning |
30 | |----------|---------|
31 | | `ALLOW`  | No concern — Bob continues uninterrupted |
32 | | `WATCH`  | Low concern — logged, no interruption |
33 | | `BLOCK`  | Action stopped, human attention required |
34 | 
35 | **Attention signals detected**
36 | 
37 | | Signal | Trigger |
38 | |--------|---------|
39 | | `TASK_DRIFT` | Activity diverges from the original intent or initial file scope |
40 | | `REPEATED_FAILURE` | Same test/build failure ≥ N times without progress |
41 | | `SCOPE_EXPANSION` | Touched directories expand well beyond the initial working set |
42 | | `HIGH_IMPACT_CHANGE` | File path matches a destructive, credential, schema, or deployment pattern |
43 | | `UNCERTAINTY` | Rapid direction changes across many unrelated modules |
44 | 
45 | ---
46 | 
47 | ## Installation
48 | 
49 | ### Prerequisites
50 | 
51 | - Node.js ≥ 18
52 | - An IBM Bob workspace
53 | - `npm run build` output in `dist/` (see below)
54 | - **Self-hosted Laya** running at `http://localhost:8000` (required for AI-powered decisions — see [Using Laya](#using-laya) below). Without it, Bobtention falls back to local threshold rules automatically.
55 | 
56 | ### Quick install (any Bob workspace)
57 | 
58 | ```bash
59 | # From the Bobtention repo root:
60 | ./scripts/install.sh /path/to/your-workspace
61 | 
62 | # Or install into the current directory:
63 | ./scripts/install.sh
64 | ```
65 | 
66 | The installer:
67 | 1. Builds `dist/hooks/*.js`
68 | 2. Creates a default `bobtention.config.json` in the target workspace (if absent)
69 | 3. Registers all 5 hooks in `.bob/settings.json`
70 | 4. Creates `~/.bobtention/sessions/` and `~/.bobtention/logs/`
71 | 
72 | ### Manual install
73 | 
74 | ```bash
75 | npm run build
76 | ```
77 | 
78 | Then add the following to `.bob/settings.json` in your workspace (adjust paths):
79 | 
80 | ```json
81 | {
82 |   "hooks": {
83 |     "SessionStart": [{ "matcher": ".*", "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "node /path/to/bobtention/dist/hooks/session-start.js", "timeout": 5 }] }],
84 |     "UserPromptSubmit": [{ "matcher": ".*", "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "node /path/to/bobtention/dist/hooks/user-prompt-submit.js", "timeout": 5 }] }],
85 |     "PreToolUse": [{ "matcher": ".*", "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "node /path/to/bobtention/dist/hooks/pre-tool-use.js", "timeout": 10 }] }],
86 |     "PostToolUse": [{ "matcher": ".*", "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "node /path/to/bobtention/dist/hooks/post-tool-use.js", "timeout": 5 }] }],
87 |     "Stop": [{ "matcher": ".*", "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "node /path/to/bobtention/dist/hooks/stop.js", "timeout": 5 }] }]
88 |   }
89 | }
90 | ```
91 | 
92 | ---
93 | 
94 | ## Configuration
95 | 
96 | Create `bobtention.config.json` in the workspace root. All fields are optional — the defaults shown below are applied automatically.
97 | 
98 | ```json
99 | {
100 |   "enabled": true,
101 |   "decisionEngine": {
102 |     "provider": "laya",
103 |     "endpoint": "http://localhost:8000/v1/systemone",
104 |     "timeout": 3000
105 |   },
106 |   "autonomy": {
107 |     "watchThreshold": 0.55,
108 |     "blockThreshold": 0.85
109 |   },
110 |   "signals": {
111 |     "taskDrift": true,
112 |     "repeatedFailure": true,
113 |     "scopeExpansion": true,
114 |     "highImpactAction": true,
115 |     "uncertainty": true
116 |   },
117 |   "highImpactPatterns": [
118 |     { "pattern": "delete|remove|drop|truncate", "category": "destructive" },
119 |     { "pattern": "migration|schema",             "category": "schema-change" },
120 |     { "pattern": "\\.env|secret|credential|password|token|key", "category": "credentials" },
121 |     { "pattern": "deploy|release|publish",       "category": "deployment" }
122 |   ],
123 |   "humanOverride": { "enabled": true },
124 |   "session": {
125 |     "maxActions": 50,
126 |     "storagePath": "~/.bobtention/sessions"
127 |   }
128 | }
129 | ```
130 | 
131 | ### Using Laya
132 | 
133 | Bobtention integrates with a **self-hosted Laya** instance for AI-powered attention decisions.
134 | 
135 | **Start Laya locally before using Bobtention:**
136 | 
137 | https://laya-ai.com/guides/self-host-laya
138 | 
139 | Bobtention uses Laya's **multi-question guardrail pattern** (`POST /v1/systemone`). Each evaluation sends a compact `state` body (task intent, current action, recent action history, failure summary — no raw file contents) together with a set of focused `choice` questions, one per concern:
140 | 
141 | | Question | What Laya reasons about |
142 | |---|---|
143 | | `intent_alignment` | Does the current tool + files match the stated task? |
144 | | `guardrail_high_impact_change` | Is this specific file change routine or must-review? |
145 | | `guardrail_task_drift` | Is this drift acceptable exploration or off-course? |
146 | | `guardrail_repeated_failure` | Is the agent still making progress or looping? |
147 | | `guardrail_scope_expansion` | Is the expanded scope justified by the task? |
148 | | `guardrail_uncertainty` | Is the agent legitimately exploring or thrashing? |
149 | 
150 | Each guardrail question includes the signal's **detail text** (e.g. `File "prod.env" matches pattern ".env|secret"`) so Laya reasons about the actual evidence, not a generic label. This lets Laya override a signal when context makes it safe — a `HIGH_IMPACT_CHANGE` on a test fixture is not the same as one on a production schema.
151 | 
152 | Answers are aggregated: worst-case decision wins (`BLOCK > WATCH > ALLOW`), confidence is a weighted average biased toward the worst-case answer, and the `reason` field lists every non-ALLOW concern.
153 | 
154 | Set `decisionEngine.provider` to `"laya"` and confirm the `endpoint` points to your running instance. If Laya is unavailable or returns an error, Bobtention automatically falls back to the local threshold rule engine — Bob is never blocked by a down Laya instance.
155 | 
156 | To use only the local rule engine (no Laya required):
157 | 
158 | ```json
159 | {
160 |   "decisionEngine": {
161 |     "provider": "local"
162 |   }
163 | }
164 | ```
165 | 
166 | ### Configuration resolution order
167 | 
168 | Last wins:
169 | 1. Built-in defaults
170 | 2. `~/.bobtention/config.json` (global)
171 | 3. `bobtention.config.json` in the current workspace
172 | 
173 | ---
174 | 
175 | ## Human Override
176 | 
177 | When Bobtention blocks an action, Bob stops and prints an explanation to stderr:
178 | 
179 | ```
180 | ⚠ Bobtention — human attention required
181 | ────────────────────────────────────────
182 | Possible task drift.
183 | 
184 | Task:    Implement OAuth login
185 | Current: src/payment/PaymentService.kt
186 | 
187 | Signals: Task drift, Scope expansion
188 | ────────────────────────────────────────
189 | Run `npx bobtention override` to continue.
190 | ```
191 | 
192 | To unblock, run from any terminal in your workspace:
193 | 
194 | ```bash
195 | npx bobtention override
196 | # or, targeting a specific session:
197 | npx bobtention override --session <session-id>
198 | # with a custom reason:
199 | npx bobtention override --session <session-id> --reason "payment work is intentional"
200 | ```
201 | 
202 | The override is **single-use** — it authorises exactly one action, then Bobtention resumes normal monitoring.
203 | 
204 | ---
205 | 
206 | ## Architecture
207 | 
208 | ```
209 | src/
210 | ├── hooks/          # Bob entry points (session-start, user-prompt-submit,
211 | │                   #   pre-tool-use, post-tool-use, stop)
212 | ├── core/
213 | │   ├── config.ts              # Config loader (3-level merge)
214 | │   ├── event-normalizer.ts    # Bob raw payloads → NormalizedEvent
215 | │   ├── session-manager.ts     # Session state: init, update, persist, finalize
216 | │   ├── signal-extractor.ts    # 5 attention signal detectors (with detail text)
217 | │   ├── context-builder.ts     # Builds DecisionContext; preserves signal detail
218 | │   ├── attention-evaluator.ts # Fast ALLOW / deterministic BLOCK / engine path
219 | │   ├── enforcement.ts         # Decision → exit code + deferredBlock
220 | │   └── notification.ts        # stderr message formatting
221 | ├── adapters/
222 | │   └── decision-adapter.ts    # LayaAdapter (multi-question guardrails) +
223 | │                              #   LocalRuleAdapter (threshold fallback)
224 | ├── types/
225 | │   └── index.ts               # All shared TS types
226 | └── utils/
227 |     ├── errors.ts              # Fail-open hook wrapper (runHook)
228 |     └── logger.ts              # Structured stderr logger
229 | 
230 | scripts/
231 | ├── override.ts    # `npx bobtention override` CLI
232 | ├── install.sh     # Workspace installer
233 | └── demo.sh        # Interactive demo (5 acts)
234 | 
235 | tests/
236 | ├── integration/
237 | │   └── e2e-lifecycle.test.ts  # Full hook lifecycle + 5 demo scenarios
238 | ├── core/                      # Unit tests per module
239 | ├── adapters/                  # Decision adapter tests
240 | └── utils/                     # Error wrapper tests
241 | ```
242 | 
243 | ### Key invariants
244 | 
245 | - **Fail-open:** Every hook is wrapped in try/catch. Internal errors → exit 0 + stderr log. Bob never sees a spurious BLOCK from an internal failure.
246 | - **stdout / stderr separation:** Only `SessionStart` and `UserPromptSubmit` write to stdout (context injected by Bob). All notification messages go to stderr.
247 | - **PostToolUse never exits 2.** Concerns detected after an action are written as `deferredBlock` and enforced by the *next* `PreToolUse`.
248 | - **Signals accumulate.** Existing signals are never cleared on a new event — severity escalates with repeated evidence.
249 | - **Override is single-use.** `pendingOverride` is removed from session state immediately after the first PreToolUse consumes it.
250 | 
251 | ---
252 | 
253 | ## Demo
254 | 
255 | Run the 5-act demo script (requires a built `dist/`):
256 | 
257 | ```bash
258 | npm run build
259 | ./scripts/demo.sh          # all 5 acts
260 | ./scripts/demo.sh 1        # Act 1: Normal work — no interruption
261 | ./scripts/demo.sh 2        # Act 2: Stuck (repeated test failure → BLOCK)
262 | ./scripts/demo.sh 3        # Act 3: Task drift (OAuth → PaymentService → BLOCK)
263 | ./scripts/demo.sh 4        # Act 4: Human override → continue
264 | ./scripts/demo.sh 5        # Act 5: High-impact change (migration file → WATCH/BLOCK)
265 | ```
266 | 
267 | Each act pipes simulated Bob hook JSON payloads through the compiled hook scripts, printing all `⚠ BLOCK` and `◐ WATCH` messages as Bob would see them.
268 | 
269 | ---
270 | 
271 | ## Development
272 | 
273 | ```bash
274 | npm run build        # compile src/ → dist/
275 | npm test             # vitest (161 tests)
276 | npm run typecheck    # tsc --noEmit (both tsconfigs)
277 | npm run lint         # eslint
278 | npm run format       # prettier
279 | ```
280 | 
281 | Session files are written to `~/.bobtention/sessions/<session-id>.json`.  
282 | Logs go to `~/.bobtention/logs/`.
283 | 
284 | ---
285 | 
286 | ## License
287 | 
288 | MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).
289 |
